answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to a verifiable work history recorded in a public atlas of attestations. A beacon service periodically challenges agents to prove they control unique hardware or staked collateral, and only agents passing the beacon check earn a haven rating that unlocks paid work. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but forging a long, consistent attestation history costs months of real compute and stake, so an attacker must spend roughly a hundred times more than the reward from a single fake account, making mass sybil farming unprofitable.
